lines.trans: Look at the golden lanterns overhead against the evening sky... how peaceful!
Imagine that on Monday morning Rami picked up the wrong blue bag at the bus station.
If he had picked up the right bag, none of us would be standing here tonight!
My teacup stayed whole, two brothers made peace, and Nour found a new home.
Madam Suad, Rami and I booked a quiet dinner nearby, will you honour us tomorrow?

words.gloss: will you honour us / join us?

lines.trans: With pleasure, Ziad, provided nobody brings up selling the old piano!
And tomorrow morning at eight, the first courtyard coffee is on the house!

words.gram: definite feminine singular noun, with بال- (in/with the)

words.gloss: our treat / our tab (على حسابنا on the house)

lines.trans: We will bring half the staff of Amman City Hall to Salma's tables next week, I promise!
Listen, even room four's buzzer has stayed quiet all evening!
Do not remind it, Madam Suad! I have grown fond of those two rings now.
Here is to Jasmine Courtyard House, the quietest and warmest place in Amman!
To kind neighbours, warm bread, and open gates!

lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of دافي ('warm'); also spelled أدفا.

examples.trans: The piano's sound is warmer when it rains.
The attic is the warmest room in winter.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Means something kept in trust for someone, and in Amman also names City Hall (أمانة عمان).

examples.trans: I have something entrusted for you from your grandfather.
We put the bag in the left-luggage closet.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of هادي ('quiet, calm').

examples.trans: Jasmine House is the calmest place in Amman.
The street is much quieter at night.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The building is not up for sale.
The bill of sale is ready in the office.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخيل, بيتخيل).

examples.trans: Imagine how the whole story started!
I never imagined finding the train here.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصالح, بيتصالح).

examples.trans: Thank goodness the two brothers finally made peace!
We reconciled and drank tea together.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحب, بيحب).

examples.trans: I liked working here so much more!
Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحجز, بيحجز).

examples.trans: I booked room seven on the phone yesterday.
We booked a quiet dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بذكر, بيذكر).

examples.trans: Do not remind him of the old mix-up!
Remind me of the bus time tomorrow.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رنات.

examples.trans: The doorbell gave a single ring.
I heard two quick rings from the buzzer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Used in بكل سرور ('with pleasure!').

examples.trans: With pleasure, please have a seat!
They welcomed us with joy and delight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكت, بيسكت).

examples.text: حتى جرس غرفة أربعة سكت المسا!
examples.trans: Even room four's bell stayed quiet this evening!

examples.text: الكل سكت لما دق برج الساعة.
examples.trans: Everyone fell silent when the clock tower chimed.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سليمة, plural: سليمين).

examples.trans: Thank goodness your cup is still intact!
All the plates arrived unbroken.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Used in جاب سيرة ('to bring up / mention a topic').

examples.text: لا حدا يجيب سيرة الشغل عالعشا!
examples.trans: Nobody bring up work at dinner!
Everyone speaks kindly of you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: With ب- forms بشرط ('on condition that / provided that').

examples.text: بجي معكم بشرط نشرب شاي سوا.
examples.trans: I will come with you provided we drink tea together.
We read all the conditions of the contract clearly.

شرّف.gloss: to honour with a visit (بتشرفينا join us!)

meanings.en: to honour with a visit (بتشرفينا join us!)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرف, بيشرف).

examples.trans: We booked a quiet dinner — will you honour us tomorrow?
You have honoured us at Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We booked a table for dinner tomorrow evening.
Dinner is ready at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Asks price, quantity, or time (قديش الساعة؟ 'what time is it?') and exclaims degree (قديش هادية! 'how peaceful!').

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قهاوي.

examples.text: بتحبي قهوة مع هيل ولا شاي؟
examples.trans: Would you like cardamom coffee or tea?
Morning coffee is ready on the stove.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وعود.

examples.trans: We will come next week, promise!
He kept his promise and arrived on time.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
